title: Arkret Account Operation DTOs
description: Closed request and response DTOs for account self-service operations, service-authenticated Account Authority PCR authoring basis discovery, and Account Authority to Principal Server account-status publication.

account_subject.description: Deployment-local, non-reversible stable account subject: SHA-256 over utf8('ak.account-subject.v1\n') followed by RFC 8785 JCS of {account_authority_id, service_account_id}. It binds one authenticated service account into the identity-root transcript without disclosing the raw local account id.

dpop_jkt.description: RFC 7638 SHA-256 JWK thumbprint of the holder key, encoded base64url without padding.

handle_claim_ref.description: Opaque reference to a signed ak.schema.handle_claim.v1 claim, such as an event ref, issuer-local receipt ref, or content-addressed artifact ref.

expires_at.description: Lease expiry. Issued lifetime MUST be no greater than 15 minutes; 15 minutes is also the v1 default.

account_registration_control_proof.description: Closed control proof for binding an already-published full_id to principal_id through account register. OIDC, passkey, or agent authentication alone is insufficient to establish DID control. The Account Authority resolves full_id at high freshness, requires project(full_id)=principal_id, and selects the current active update key of the entry pinned by did_version_id from verified method history rather than from request-supplied key material. The signature covers every field except signature as canonical JSON with domain separator ak.account-registration-control-proof-v1 and MUST replay the durable challenge issued by ak.gate.account.command.issue_did_binding_challenge.

request_canonical_digest.description: SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the complete account_register_request_body with proof.request_canonical_digest and proof.signature omitted.

account_subject.description: Service account subject this identity is being bound to. Signed so the proof cannot be replayed to bind the same identity to a different account.

principal_id.description: Stable core_id echoed by the challenge and equal to project(full_id).

full_id.description: Complete DID resolved by the Account Authority and signed by the holder; it MUST equal the register request full_id byte-for-byte.

did_version_id.description: Adapter-defined versionId of the entry whose current active update key signed this proof.

control_key_digest.description: SHA-256 over the canonical multikey bytes of the verified current active update key.

dpop_jkt.description: DPoP holder thumbprint echoed by the durable challenge.

expires_at.description: Issued lifetime MUST be no greater than 300 seconds.

verification_method.description: Current active update-key DID URL under full_id. The verifier parses its bare DID component with the registered adapter and requires the projected core_id to equal principal_id; it never appends a fragment to principal_id.

witness_evidence.description: Method-native witness / freshness evidence digest for the external DID, required by deployments that do not host the DID themselves.

account_handoff_authentication_proof.description: OIDC authorization-code exchange proof used only to create a DPoP-bound account handoff. The signature is made by the same Ed25519 holder key as the request DPoP proof over utf8('ak.account-handoff-authentication-proof-v1\n') || RFC8785_JCS(this object with signature omitted).

challenge.description: Account Authority-generated challenge persisted with the OIDC authorization transaction and consumed by this exchange.

request_canonical_digest.description: sha256:<lowercase-hex> of SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the complete account_handoff_request_body with proof.request_canonical_digest and proof.signature omitted.

signature.description: 64-byte Ed25519 signature encoded base64url without padding.

reserved_identity_creation.description: Server-persisted identity-creation checkpoint, readable only by the authenticated current holder of the owning service account's identity-creation lease. It is NOT public: an unfinished reservation would otherwise leak that a specific account is mid-registration, and abandoning it would leave a permanent public trace. Once registration completes the public artifact is the published DID log entry itself, so this checkpoint never needs to become public. It contains the exact unpublished or already-published DID operation, never recovery words, seed material, private keys, or an encrypted root export.

operation_digest.description: sha256:<lowercase-hex> of SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the complete did_operation object.

expires_at.description: Lease expiry. Issued lifetime MUST be no greater than 15 minutes; 15 minutes is also the v1 default.

reserved_identity.description: Holder-authenticated identity-creation checkpoint carried while a reservation exists. It MUST be omitted once the provisional identity has been explicitly abandoned through ak.gate.account.command.abandon_identity_creation: after abandonment the checkpoint MUST NOT remain readable on this or any other holder-readable surface, because leaving it would keep publishing that some account once tried to create an identity. That is a security property, not a cleanup policy.

expires_at.description: Expiry of the conflicting live identity-creation lease. The client uses this authenticated upper bound for waiting UI; it conveys no holder identity or authority.

account_handle.description: Canonical handle of the authenticated service account. This unsigned UX hint is only for display and local artifact naming; it MUST NOT be treated as principal identity evidence, authorization, or a service-account-to-principal binding.

account_subject.description: Stable subject for the authenticated service account. The client freezes this value from the DPoP-bound handoff and MUST require the identity-binding challenge to echo it byte-for-byte before signing.

preferred_locale.description: Optional private UI-language preference of the authenticated service account. It is returned only in this DPoP-bound handoff response so the client can continue the just-completed authentication flow in the selected language; it MUST NOT be copied into a public actor profile.

account_handoff_grant.description: Opaque, short-lived credential bound to the request DPoP key. It is not ak.session.grant and has no refresh-token semantics.

allowed_operations.description: Closed set of operations this handoff may be presented at. The two abandonment operations are members because a never-accepted PCR leaves the holder without a principal, so no principal-bound ak.session.grant can carry them; membership here does not widen the handoff into a session credential.

full_id.description: Complete standard DID whose registered method adapter MUST project to the principal_id derived from did_operation.

identity_binding_challenge_outcome.description: Persisted, single-use server challenge. The client copies every field from challenge_id through expires_at into identity_creation_control_proof, adds proof_kind and verification_key_multibase, and signs that complete proof object with signature omitted. request_id is idempotency metadata and is not part of the root-control transcript.

operation_digest.description: sha256:<lowercase-hex> of SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the complete request did_operation object.

did_version_id.description: Validated did:webvh inception versionId copied into the root-control transcript.

log_head_digest.description: SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the exact method-native inception log entry.

control_key_digest.description: SHA-256 over the canonical multikey bytes of the current active update key (parameters.updateKeys[0]) of the DID entry pinned by did_version_id; never private key material or a next-key commitment. For account-first inception that entry is entry 0; for an already-published DID it is the entry current at binding time, so a spent inception key is never required.

pcr_genesis_unit_kinds.description: Closed ordered declaration copied into the identity-root creation transcript.

identity_creation_control_proof.description: Fresh proof signed by the did:webvh inception operation's parameters.updateKeys[0] identity root. The verifier selects that key from did_operation and MUST NOT treat a request-supplied key or a DID Document verificationMethod as authority. Signature covers every field except signature as canonical JSON with domain separator ak.identity-creation-control-proof-v1.

pcr_realm_id.description: Principal Control Realm id obtained only by retyping the exact root-signed ak.realm.create event_id; it is not derived from principal_id and MUST equal the pcr_genesis_unit create Event's retyped id.

realm_create_payload_digest.description: Canonical digest of the ak.realm.create payload only. Event ids and envelope digests are forbidden from this transcript.

founding_authorize_payload_digest.description: Canonical digest of the founding ak.device.authorize payload only. Event ids and envelope digests are forbidden from this transcript.

initial_session_request_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of RFC 8785 JCS InitialSessionGrantRequest. The embedded session_public_key MUST thumbprint to dpop_jkt; this binds the first Standard grant intent without turning it into a separate root-signed object.

signature.description: 64-byte Ed25519 identity-root signature encoded base64url without padding.

binding_kind.description: Discriminates the already-published DID proof branch from account-first identity creation.

full_id.description: Verified complete DID whose registered adapter projects to principal_id.

did_version_id.description: Adapter-defined version identifier pinned when the account binding was accepted.

control_key_digest.description: Digest of the verified current control key that authorized this binding.

identity_creation_lease_id.description: Present only when binding_kind=identity_creation. The published_did branch creates no identity-creation lease.

head_event_digest.description: DID registry log head digest for the exact did:webvh inception entry accepted during this binding saga; it is not a PCR Event head.

proof.description: Account Authority detached proof. payload_digest is SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the complete receipt with proof omitted, including binding_kind, principal_id, full_id, did_version_id, control_key_digest, operation/head digests, and the identity-creation lease/fence only when that branch applies. JWS signs canonical_json({context:'ak.account-binding-receipt-proof-v1', payload_digest, account_authority_id, account_subject, principal_id, full_id, did_version_id, control_key_digest, verification_method, created_at}); proof.created_at MUST equal issued_at and verification_method MUST be an assertion method of account_authority_id valid at issued_at.

propertyNames.description: ak.self.account.command.update_profile only accepts display_name, avatar_blob_ref, and profile_fields.<key>. The bio is carried as profile_fields.bio.

is_server_admin.description: True when the authenticated principal is a deployment server administrator (the server's configured admin principal set). Operator-only product surfaces (e.g. organization creation) gate their UI on this. Reducer/config-derived, not a stored account field; absent or false means non-admin.

account_register_request_body.description: Canonical account binding request. Exactly one branch is required: proof binds an already-published full_id, while identity_creation carries the account-first DID operation and PCR genesis unit. In either branch every repeated principal_id and full_id in the selected proof/creation objects and genesis initial_resolution MUST equal the outer values byte-for-byte, and the Account Authority MUST independently require project(full_id)=principal_id before any write.

full_id.description: Required for both externally created and account-first identities. The server verifies the method evidence and project(full_id)=principal_id before persisting the PCR resolution state.

account_status_authority_evidence.description: Account Authority-signed, transport-only evidence binding one service account, principal, Principal Control Realm and authorized Event issuer. It is not a public identity fact and MUST be disclosed only to Principal Servers that already hold or are about to hold state for this account/principal. The proof uses context ak.account_status.authority_evidence.v1 and payload_digest over RFC 8785 JCS of every field except proof.

binding_version.description: Monotonic Account Authority-local binding generation. A receiver MUST reject rollback relative to evidence already accepted for the same (account_authority_id, account_id).

authority_ref.description: Account Authority DID service/delegation URL authorizing issuer_service_id to sign ak.account.status for this account. For a direct Account Authority issuer this is its own account-authority service entry; for a delegated Principal Server it is the live delegation entry.

account_status_publication.description: Constrained carrier for exactly one ak.account.status Event. Initial Account Authority publication carries event only; fanout of an already accepted Event carries the same event plus account_status_receipts. AuthorizationLease and generic IngressReceipt are forbidden because this high-risk status publication is admitted against current authority state.

account_status_receipt.description: Principal Server-signed transport receipt proving that one ak.account.status Event was accepted into that receiver's local account-status frontier. It is not an offline-publication IngressReceipt, contains no AuthorizationLease id, and grants no authority. proof uses context ak.account_status.ingress_receipt.v1 and payload_digest over RFC 8785 JCS of every field except proof.

cba_proof_bundles.description: Receiver-relative Principal Control Realm CBA closure for receipted fanout. Initial publication MAY omit it when the destination already has the current PCR dependencies.

account_status_authoring_basis_request_b.description: Service-authenticated, read-only request for the exact actor-chain and Principal Control Realm Seal frontiers needed to author one ak.account.status Event. The signed authority evidence is verified before any frontier is disclosed.

account_status_authoring_basis_outcome.description: PCR-bound authoring coordinates for one authoritative account-status producer. actor_frontier supplies actor_seq and prev_refs; seal_frontier supplies the sole seal_basis leaf. Both variants MUST exactly match authority_evidence and are read-only observations, not authority grants.

account_status_publication_outcome.description: Durable operation state. accepted/duplicate are terminal for this receiver's account-status frontier; pending_seal is retryable with the same Idempotency-Key and byte-identical request until the Event is accepted or rejected. propagation_state reports this receiver's downstream fanout obligation without mutating the signed Event payload.

did_binding_challenge_request_body.description: Request a single-use challenge for binding an ALREADY-PUBLISHED full_id to principal_id. Unlike identity_binding_challenge_request_body this carries no unpublished did_operation and no PCR genesis digests: the DID already exists, and the Account Authority resolves full_id at high freshness, requires project(full_id)=principal_id, and never attempts to resolve core_id directly.

principal_id.description: Stable core_id to bind. It is not directly resolvable.

full_id.description: Already-published complete DID. The Account Authority MUST resolve it at the high freshness tier, require project(full_id)=principal_id, and MUST NOT accept caller-supplied DID history.

did_binding_challenge_outcome.description: Persisted, single-use server challenge for binding an already-published full_id to principal_id. The client copies every field from challenge_id through expires_at into account_registration_control_proof, adds proof_kind, request_canonical_digest and verification_method, and signs the closed proof with the current active update key of the entry pinned by did_version_id. The client MUST byte-compare principal_id, full_id and every other echoed field against what it expects before signing and MUST fail closed on any mismatch. request_id is idempotency metadata and is not part of the signed transcript.

account_subject.description: Service account subject that will own the binding. Signed so the proof cannot be replayed against another account.

full_id.description: Server-resolved full_id echoed into the signed proof transcript; it MUST project to principal_id.

did_version_id.description: versionId of the entry the Account Authority resolved as current; the proof MUST be signed by that entry's active update key.

witness_evidence.description: Method-native witness / freshness evidence digest resolved for this DID. Deployments that do not host the DID MUST require it: same-origin trust between registry and Principal Server does not extend to third-party DIDs.

expires_at.description: Issued lifetime MUST be no greater than 300 seconds.

identity_abandonment_challenge_request_b.description: Request the single-use challenge that makes abandoning a provisional identity explicit. It applies only while the Principal Control Realm was never accepted and the identity root is lost, so the caller can sign nothing and the account handoff grant is the only available credential. principal_id and did_version_id pin exactly which reservation is being given up.

principal_id.description: Provisional principal recorded in the holder-authenticated reserved_identity_creation checkpoint. The Account Authority MUST reject any other value and MUST NOT issue a challenge for a principal whose PCR is already accepted.

did_version_id.description: versionId of the published entry 0 that becomes the orphan anchor. Pinning it lets the confirmation detect a PCR acceptance that landed after the challenge was issued instead of abandoning a live identity.

identity_abandonment_consequence_disclos.description: Closed ordered set of consequences the client MUST present before it may submit the confirmation. The protocol fixes which consequences must be disclosed; the localized wording is deployment-owned. This list is not a self-asserted acknowledgement receipt, which would be forgeable; the anti-automation property comes from the challenge itself, which no login, session resume, lease fence advance or other automated flow ever fetches.

identity_abandonment_challenge_outcome.description: Persisted, single-use server challenge for provisional identity abandonment. It is the evidence that the abandonment was an explicit user action: the identity root is lost, so the holder cannot sign a confirmation. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states.

lease_fence.description: Identity-creation lease fence at issuance. The confirmation MUST be rejected when the current fence differs, so a concurrent holder cannot have its reservation abandoned underneath it.

expires_at.description: MUST be at most 300 seconds after issued_at.

identity_abandonment_request_body.description: Confirm the explicit abandonment of a provisional identity. It MUST present a fresh account handoff grant and MUST NOT reuse the grant presented when the challenge was issued; how strong the authentication behind that fresh handoff is, which risk checks run and how long any cooldown lasts are deployment governance and are deliberately not specified here.

request_id.description: Idempotency identity of the abandonment. Replaying it returns the recorded terminal outcome and MUST NOT produce a second orphan-anchor tombstone.

identity_abandonment_outcome.description: Recorded terminal outcome of an explicit abandonment. One transaction consumed the challenge, recorded the orphan-anchor tombstone / audit reservation, suppressed the reserved_identity_creation checkpoint on every holder-readable surface and released the identity-creation lease. There is exactly one success terminal; every other terminal is an error reply. Whether the orphan anchor is annotated on a discovery surface, when its handle and namespace are released and how long the reservation is retained are deployment governance and are not carried here.

principal_id.description: The abandoned provisional principal. Its published entry 0 is now a permanently unusable orphan anchor: it MUST NOT be reused and continuity MUST NOT be claimed over it.
